case.title: Tar balls on Goa beaches traced to an offshore oil rig
case.subRegion: Goa beaches, Arabian Sea (source offshore, unidentified at time of deposition)

oil.spilledNote: Weathered crude residues (tar balls). NIO multi-marker fingerprinting matched an offshore oil rig.

facilities.name: MUMBAI HIGH OFFSHORE FIELD
facilities.note: Candidate only. NIO matched 'an offshore oil rig' (not named in the reporting used here); Bombay High was the identified source for 2012 Gujarat tar balls.

observations.description: Tar balls deposited along Goa beaches (southwest monsoon onset season)

timeline.event: Tar balls collected along Goa coast
NIO study (Vasimalla et al.) matches fingerprints to an offshore oil rig

case.officialFindings: Chemical fingerprinting matched May 2017 Goa tar balls to an offshore oil rig. No vessel identified.

sources.title: Tarballs dot India's west coast annually (Mongabay India, Nov 2022)
Identifying the source of tar balls on Goa beaches in 2013 (NIO fingerprinting method, PubMed)

sarMeasurements.method: Adaptive-threshold dark-spot detection on Lee-filtered calibrated backscatter (classical method, not a trained model)
limitations: Dark spots include look-alikes (low wind, biogenic films, rain cells); the look-alike checks must still be applied
Land is masked with a coastline plus a coastal buffer; detections within a few km of shore remain unreliable
Multilooking trades resolution for speckle reduction; slicks narrower than two output pixels can be missed
The quicklook is in radar geometry (not north-up); use the outlines on the map for location
